name: African American community and Rosenwald school building

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated funding arrangement in the cited historical account; later construction and program expansion are distinct.

caveats: These schools operated within racially segregated, unequal public systems. Matching arrangements shifted burdens onto Black residents and required white public officials’ cooperation; a grant does not establish attendance or equal access. Educational work by Black communities long preceded this program. The 1912 initial arrangement and 1913 financial assistance precede completion of all six buildings; published accounts vary in how they date the start.

research.note: Independent review checked the initial funding chronology and the later expansion amount against NPS historical accounts; dates of completion remain distinct.
